name: Sage Accounting
tagline: Cloud accounting, invoicing, bank reconciliation, reporting, and payroll add-ons

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Sage Accounting's durable value is banking, compliance, trust, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a private small-business accounting ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: CSV exports from the user's own accounts
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations
live bank feeds and payment rails
whyPeopleStillPay: Sage Accounting: People pay because errors touch real money. Bank connections, reconciliation, tax changes, evidence, security, and support are the product.
ongoingBurden: Own data integrity, backups, import mapping, reconciliation, security, audit logs, tax changes, and recovery.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Local-first open-source personal finance and envelope budgeting.

priorArt.name: Invoice Ninja
priorArt.desc: Open-source invoicing, payments, and client management.

alternatives.name: Pandle Free
alternatives.desc: UK books, invoices and MTD returns for free; live bank feeds, receipt capture and mileage are the £5 temptation.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser; no card is required for the free plan
facts.dataFormat: Books, invoices, contacts, tax records, and imported statements live in Pandle's cloud database; reports and accounting data can be exported, but the internal storage format is not disclosed.
facts.gapVsPaid: Pandle Free omits the live bank feeds, receipt capture, mileage tracking, project tools, and payroll ecosystem that make Sage's paid cloud workflow more automatic.
facts.setupBlocker: The account is easy to open, but a non-expert still has to enter opening balances, choose the correct UK VAT/MTD settings, and import or reconcile historical transactions.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Accounting, invoices, reconciliation, reporting and payroll in one ERP; local filing still needs local judgment.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext can cover the ledger and payroll, but it is far harder to configure and lacks Sage's turnkey UK bank feeds, MTD guidance, support, and payroll add-on experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A full desktop ledger with bank reconciliation and invoices; cloud collaboration did not make the installer.

facts.install: Native desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.dataFormat: Each business is stored in a local .manager file backed by SQLite, including its accounting records and attached documents; the user chooses and backs up that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Manager Desktop is effectively a local single-user company file, so it gives up Sage's managed bank connections, browser collaboration, payroll add-ons, and automatic cloud operation.

alternatives.name: Bigcapital
alternatives.desc: Modern double-entry accounting and inventory in Docker; automatic bank feeds are not included.

facts.install: Official server setup script and Docker-based deployment
facts.dataFormat: Books, contacts, invoices, bills, inventory, and settings live in the deployment's MariaDB database, with generated files and attachments on configured server storage.
facts.gapVsPaid: Bigcapital lacks Sage's plug-and-play bank feeds, UK tax and MTD workflow, payroll add-ons, and accountant ecosystem, while making the user operate the server.
facts.setupBlocker: It needs a Linux server, Docker, DNS and HTTPS, database and mail configuration, backups, and upgrades; the hosted product is not the indefinitely free path.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Books, invoices, bank accounts, stock and reports without a subscription; the UI is all business.

facts.install: Docker Compose is the shortest documented path; packages and manual Perl installation also exist
facts.dataFormat: Companies and accounting records live in PostgreSQL databases; uploaded or generated documents live in the configured document store or server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: LedgerSMB's accounting core is strong, but its interface, bank automation, UK filing guidance, payroll integration, mobile access, and hosted support are materially rougher than Sage's.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real web stack, Docker, PostgreSQL, administrator credentials, a reverse proxy and TLS for internet use, plus backups and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Odoo Accounting (One App Free)
alternatives.desc: Hosted accounting for zero dollars and unlimited users; adding a second unrelated app ends the free plan.

facts.install: Create an Odoo Online database and select Accounting as the single free app
facts.dataFormat: Accounting records and attachments live in the Odoo Online database and filestore operated by Odoo; the internal storage format is not exposed to the hosted user.
facts.gapVsPaid: Odoo's one-app-free accounting database is less straightforward for a small UK business, and adding payroll or another separate Odoo app ends the genuinely free plan.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is configuring the correct country localization, chart of accounts, taxes, journals, and bank import; installing any additional priced Odoo app ends One App Free eligibility.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoicing, banking, stock and accounting in one practical suite; payroll is outside the core project.

facts.install: DoliWamp, DoliDeb, DoliRPM, Docker, or a conventional PHP web-server installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records live in MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, while uploaded and generated documents live in Dolibarr's documents directory or mounted volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dolibarr covers books and stock but does not provide Sage's polished UK bank-feed, MTD, payroll, and accountant workflow out of the box.
facts.setupBlocker: A packaged desktop-style installer exists on some platforms, but a durable deployment still needs a web server or Docker, database, HTTPS, backups, updates, and localization.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Double-entry books, reconciliation and reports on the desktop; cloud convenience is replaced by file ownership.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or operating-system package
facts.dataFormat: The default book is a local compressed XML .gnucash file; SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends are optional, but the documentation warns that database storage does not make GnuCash a true multi-user application.
facts.gapVsPaid: GnuCash replaces Sage's shared cloud workspace with a desktop file and lacks managed bank feeds, payroll, mobile collaboration, and guided UK tax filing.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Adminsoft Accounts
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The famous free UK answer stopped being free for new releases on 25 July 2026, so the no-cost build is now the frozen one.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Akaunting
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free base is single-entry unless you buy the Double-Entry app, and the repo is BSL rather than open source.

notes: Credibility row: Sage Accounting survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Sage Accounting; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a private small-business accounting ledger that imports user-supplied CSV files, categorizes entries, reconciles balances, and exports reports.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: audited security and recovery; multi-user controls and accountant workflows; bank, payment, tax, and reconciliation integrations.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
discontinued: was retired in the US on December 31, 2024, with support ending January 31, 2025; Sage still sells it in the UK and other countries
